definitions: A comparator circuit that incorporates positive feedback to implement hysteresis, preventing noisy input signals from causing rapid oscillation of the output.
A bistable electronic circuit that converts an analog input signal into a digital output signal, characterized by different threshold levels for rising and falling inputs.
examples: The Schmitt trigger is essential for debouncing switches.
We used a Schmitt trigger to clean up the sensor output.
The hysteresis of the Schmitt trigger prevents false triggering.
